verification_method: osv.dev /v1/query, with every returned advisory re-checked against its own affected ranges

findings.tests: GIT HISTORY SCANNING - absent from the working tree at HEAD, still present in history
findings.notes: VERIFIED at build time: a working-tree scan (`gitleaks dir`) reports 0 findings for this file; a history scan (`gitleaks git`) reports 1, at backend/app/settlement.py:16 in commit 5f9ec864. The file does not exist at HEAD. A scanner that only walks the filesystem misses this entirely and is wrong. ARVE must not mark it RESOLVED merely because HEAD is clean - the credential was committed and must be treated as exposed until rotated. Its value is derived deterministically by seed_history.py rather than written there as a literal, precisely so the build script does not itself put the secret at HEAD and destroy this test.

findings.tests: FINGERPRINT BEHAVIOUR - one finding or two? Whatever ARVE does must be deliberate
findings.notes: Same 48-char value at backend/app/config.py:45 and backend/tests/conftest.py:14. Gitleaks reports TWO findings because it fingerprints per (file, line, secret). If ARVE dedupes on secret_hash alone it will report ONE; if it includes file path it will report TWO. Both are defensible - but the choice must be intentional and consistent, because it determines whether fixing one file resolves the finding or leaves it OPEN.

findings.tests: LINE-INDEPENDENT secret_hash IDENTITY - must report the same finding, not resolve-and-reopen

That noise is what trains people to ignore the tool.

findings.tests: ambiguous by design - exercises the FALSE_POSITIVE / SUPPRESSED lifecycle
findings.notes: VERIFIED: gitleaks DOES report this despite the .example filename - it is not path-suppressed by default. So the ambiguity is not resolved by the scanner, it is pushed to triage. findings.tests: LIFECYCLE: a secret ROTATED IN PLACE - old value history-only, new value at HEAD, both on the same line
findings.notes: The value at HEAD is the post-rotation key. An earlier commit carries a DIFFERENT key at the SAME line of the SAME file (the rotation is made deliberately in its own commit in Phase 5; the old value is derived from a fixed seed by seed_history.py and never appears at HEAD). EXPECTED DIVERGENCE, not a bug in the plant: reference `gitleaks git` reports TWO findings (old value and new value, both at line 14, in different commits), while ARVE reports ONE finding that stays continuously OPEN and never observes the rotation at all - it scans only HEAD, and the dir-mode fingerprint file:rule:line is identical before and after, so a replaced credential is indistinguishable from an untouched one. This is the mirror image of SEC-06 (same value, different line -> looks like a NEW finding) and the complement of SEC-22 (different values, same line -> collapse). See ARVE_ISSUES.md issue 3.

scanner_limitations.summary: A Mapbox public token inside a URL is not matched by mapbox-api-token; only generic-api-key fires (via 'access_token=').
scanner_limitations.cause: The rule regex requires the literal keyword 'mapbox' followed only by [ \t\w.-]{0,20} and optional quotes before an assignment operator (= : => , etc). In a URL the word 'mapbox' is separated from '=' by '/' and '?', so the keyword context can never match.
scanner_limitations.consequence: A Mapbox token leaked in a CSS/HTML URL is reported under generic-api-key (rule attribution lost) and only because the query parameter name contains 'token'.

scanner_limitations.summary: A Google API key followed by '&' (i.e. not the last query parameter) is not detected by any rule.
scanner_limitations.cause: The rule regex requires the 39-char key to be followed by one of [`'" \t\n;], a literal \n / \r escape, or end of line. '&' is not in that set, and [\w-] stops at '&', so the match fails.
scanner_limitations.consequence: Google's own documented script-tag order (key first, callback second) is invisible to gitleaks. Not planted, because only detectable flaws are planted.
scanner_limitations.also_noted: gcp-api-key's entropy threshold rose from 3 (8.24.2) to 4 (8.30.1); random keys clear both.

scanner_limitations.summary: StartColumn is wrong for a secret deep inside a very long single line, and differs between gitleaks versions.
scanner_limitations.cause: Most likely dir-mode chunked reading: the column is computed relative to the chunk, not the line. Line number is correct.

tooling_notes.issue: stamp_commit_references() could never rewrite a stale commit hash
tooling_notes.detail: The substitution pattern contained two literal BACKSPACE bytes (0x08) where the source should have read backslash-b (a regex word boundary): re.sub(r'<BS>[0-9a-f]{7,40}<BS>', ...). A terminal erases the preceding character when it prints a backspace, so every listing of the file - including inspect.getsource - displayed a correct-looking pattern. The regex matched nothing, so the rewrite loop found no changes and the function returned False while still printing the mappings it had computed. Present since the original build (commit b8333656) and never noticed, because the rewrite path only runs when a quoted hash actually changes, which never happened until SEC-27 introduced hashes that move on every rebuild. Fixed 2026-09-22; the rebuild now stamps SEC-27's two commits correctly.
tooling_notes.how_it_was_found: a scratch-clone rebuild failed its own final assertion: the answer key still quoted commits that were not ancestors of HEAD

tooling_notes.issue: what a --force rebuild does and does not reproduce
tooling_notes.detail: VERIFIED by rebuilding a scratch clone and diffing: commits 1-10 come out BYTE-IDENTICAL, which covers every commit hash this answer key quotes for SEC-04 (5f9ec864, 5c1f6a8f) and SEC-06 (4da4e7e2, dc9a9d69) as well as the baseline commits 599397be and 93db3f27. Commits 11 onward stage files this project keeps editing (both answer keys, the baselines, seed_history.py), so their hashes follow the current content and DO change; SEC-27's two commits sit in that range and are re-stamped automatically. Two things are load-bearing for the 1-10 guarantee: core.autocrlf is pinned to 'input' by the script, and README.md - which is committed in commit 1 - is embedded as README_V1 rather than read from the working tree.
tooling_notes.how_it_was_found: Phase 0 sensitivity testing: editing README.md changed every hash, as did running with core.autocrlf=false
